sections.content:
The indicator is at [[7, 41], [7, 45]], which is under the purple square (right square in legend, cols 42-44). The legend shows the indicator under the white square (left square in legend, cols 36-38).
So the current state has:
- Square: purple-over-white (purple top, white bottom)
- Indicator: under purple square
The legend shows:
- Left square: white-over-purple (white top, purple bottom)
- Indicator: under white square
I need to reverse both the square's split and the indicator's position.
To move the indicator to the white square, I need to select the white tool. But when I select the white tool and press SPACE, the square becomes all white.
Wait, maybe I don't need to press SPACE after selecting the white tool. Maybe I just need to select the white tool (move the indicator) and then press SPACE with the rectangle being purple.
Let me try:
1. Select white tool (moves indicator to white square, rectangle becomes white)
2. Press SPACE (rectangle was white, square becomes ???)
But when I select the white tool, the rectangle becomes white. Then when I press SPACE, the square becomes all white (because the tool color and rectangle color are both white).
Hmm, this is tricky. Let me try a different approach:
1. Select white tool (moves indicator to white square, rectangle becomes white)
2. Press LEFT or RIGHT to change the rectangle's shape (but keep it white)
3. Press SPACE
But the rectangle's color is determined by the selected tool, so it will be white. And when I press SPACE with the white tool selected, the square becomes all white.
Wait, maybe the issue is that I need to select the white tool without changing the rectangle's color. Let me check if clicking on the white square in the legend changes the rectangle's color.
Actually, when I select a tool by clicking on the legend's square, the rectangle's color changes to the selected tool's color. So if I click on the white square, the rectangle becomes white.
But I want the rectangle to remain purple while the indicator moves to the white square. This seems impossible with the current mechanics.
Let me try a different approach. Maybe I need to:
1. Have the rectangle be white
2. Select the purple tool
3. Press SPACE
This should make the rectangle purple and the square purple-over-white. But the indicator will be under the purple square, not the white square.
Wait, maybe the indicator's position doesn't matter. Maybe the goal is just to have the square match the legend's left square (white-over-purple).
But I can't get white-over-purple with the current mechanics. The purple tool always produces purple-over-white, and the white tool always produces all white.
Let me try a completely different approach. Maybe I need to click on the square directly to paint it. Let me try clicking on the top half of the square with the white tool selected, and then clicking on the bottom half with the purple tool selected.
Actually, let me first check if clicking on the square with a tool selected paints the square. Earlier, when I clicked on the square with the purple tool selected, the rectangle became purple but the square remained all white. So clicking on the square doesn't paint it.
Hmm, let me try pressing SPACE multiple times to see if the square's pattern cycles through different states.
Actually, let me try a different rectangle shape. Maybe there are more than 2 shapes (diamond and frame). Let me check if pressing LEFT/RIGHT cycles through more shapes.
